conviction_note: Mildly constructive: H1 adjusted EPS of $1.25 against a raised FY guide of $2.30-2.40 implies an H2 below H1 even after normal Q3 seasonality, and two direct-tier counterparties (Collins commercial OE +23%, GE Aerospace supplier material input up double digits) raised guides on Oct 20. But the quarterly consensus could not be sourced, the last guide raise (Jul 29) was sold -2.56%, and the stock has rebounded +5.6% over 20 days with the sector. So p_up is only 55 on an abs move of 5.0 (median own reaction 4.34, nudged up because a guide update is likely), giving +0.5. The findings sum to +1.4 because each is sized alone; the gap is the reaction-function veto, not an inconsistency.
bar: Company FY2026 guide, raised Jul 29, 2026: sales $2.025-2.125B, adj EPS $2.30-2.40, FCF >$195M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/717605/000119312526323808/hxl-ex99_1.htm). No Q3 consensus EPS or sales could be sourced (web search budget exhausted, so no estimate pages were reached), so the quarterly bar is UNSOURCED and every finding that depends on it is capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is a sales read against my own seasonal extrapolation (~$495M: Q2 2026 $529.3M x the Q3/Q2 2025 ratio of 456.2/489.9), not against a street number.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,785,561 shares, 6.45% of float, 4.9 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30, up 9.0% from 4,390,752 on 2026-09-15 (MarketBeat, from FINRA's 2026-10-09 release: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/HXL/short-interest/). Moderate and building, not crowded. The baseline's 25-delta skew is +1.23 vol points, i.e. balanced, but the chain is not usable (ATM spread 94% of mid, total OI 98), so the option market makes no directional statement and there is no implied move. Run-up is +5.61% over 20d and +3.66% over 5d. The stock is -17.5% from its 52-week high ($110.28 week of Jul 20), and that drawdown tracked the sector: from the week of Aug 10 to the week of Oct 5, Airbus fell 215.40 -> 187.80 EUR and Boeing 231.67 -> 190.37 (Yahoo weekly bars).

findings.finding: Hexcel's own numbers make the raised FY2026 adj-EPS guide ($2.30-2.40) look conservative. H1 2026 adjusted EPS was $1.25 (Q1 $0.59 + Q2 $0.66), so the guide implies only $1.05-1.15 for H2. Applying 2025's seasonality (Q3 $0.37 and Q4 $0.52 against Q2 $0.50, derived from FY $1.76) to Q2 2026's $0.66 gives about $0.49 + $0.69 = $1.18 for H2, or FY about $2.43, above the top of the range. A second raise or a firm-to-top is therefore more likely than not. Where the street's FY number sits could not be sourced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide raised with a beat on 2026-07-29: -2.56% (the stock had run to $110). Q1 2026 beat with the guide reaffirmed on 2026-04-22: +4.78%. Initial 2026 guide on 2026-01-28: +5.40%. On 2025-10-22, results came with a $350M ASR: +11.31%. Guidance raises have not reliably been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: sell-side models do this arithmetic. If a raise to about $2.40+ were fully in, the stock would not sit 17% below its July high on a sector de-rating with balanced skew. It has only rebounded 5.6% off its Oct 9 low ($84.96), in line with Airbus, which says no Hexcel-specific raise is being bid. The 2025 seasonal base is depressed by A350 destocking (Q4 2025 release), so the seasonal haircut may be too large, which cuts toward a raise.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 adj EPS from a separate release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/717605/000119312526170559/hxl-ex99_1.htm. The 2025 quarterly base comes from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/717605/000119312526027293/hxl-ex99_1.htm. All three are Hexcel documents. No outside source confirms the street's bar.

findings.finding: RTX's Q3 2026 release (Oct 20, after Hexcel last spoke) reports Collins Aerospace commercial OE sales +23% YoY on 'higher volume on narrowbody and widebody platforms' and raises FY2026 adjusted sales to $97.0-97.5B (from $95.0-96.0B). That is a direct read of OEM build rates in Q3 above Hexcel's own Q2 commercial aero growth of +18.3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hexcel's commercial aero growth surprise has been bought when the guide also moved up (Q1 2026 +18.8% commercial aero: +4.78%) and sold when the stock was extended (Q2 2026 +18.3%: -2.56%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since Oct 20, so aerospace investors have seen it. HXL is up only modestly since (91.32 weekly close, week of Oct 19, against 90.22 the week before), and the sealed spot is $90.95, flat with that. A full Hexcel read-through would show as HXL outrunning Airbus that week, and it has not. Pratt & Whitney commercial OE fell 5% on engine mix, so the signal is not uniform.
findings.independence: Proxy: a direct-tier supplier on the same Airbus and Boeing programmes, not Hexcel's own number. Points the same way as GE Aerospace's Oct 20 release (https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-announces-third-quarter-2026-results), which is a different company and document.

findings.finding: GE Aerospace's Q3 2026 (Oct 20) raised CES FY guide (revenue growth to low 20s from ~20%, operating profit to $10.5-10.6B from $10.25-10.35B) and said material input from priority suppliers rose by double digits YoY. LEAP deliveries were only +5% and total engine deliveries +8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Hexcel-specific history on engine-supplier read-throughs. Hexcel's commercial aero is mostly airframe (A350, 787, A320neo, 737 MAX), and engine content is a minority.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a day and mostly a services story. Engine-material input growth is a supply-chain signal that would show as aerostructure and material suppliers trading up on Oct 20-21, and nothing in HXL's sealed spot or 5-day run-up isolates that.
findings.independence: Proxy; separate company from RTX (finding 2). It is weaker on the airframe line Hexcel trades on: LEAP +5% is lukewarm.

findings.finding: Boeing delivered 22 787s in Q3 2026 against 40 in H1 (20 a quarter), 62 YTD, and the FAA certified the 737-10 on Oct 20. This is a mild uptick in widebody output on a programme Hexcel's CEO said in Q2 was at its highest sales since before the pandemic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. Deliveries lag Hexcel's material shipments by months, so this confirms the ramp rather than the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since Oct 13 and widely followed. Boeing's stock was flat over the week (190.21 -> 190.47), so the market did not read it as a rate step-up. Small, because it is a lagging counterparty number.
findings.independence: Boeing's own document. The 737-10 certification is in a separate Boeing release of 2026-10-20 (https://boeing.mediaroom.com/news-releases-statements).

findings.finding: Airbus delivered 72 aircraft in September 2026 and 547 YTD through September. Its cumulative A350 deliveries stood at 737 at end-September. Orders in October included Avolon's 110 aircraft (35 A330-900, 75 A320neo) and ACG's 75 A320neo, plus a Biman A350 order.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. Hexcel's largest customer is Airbus (A350 is its biggest single programme), but deliveries lag Hexcel shipments.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and followed. No YoY family split could be read here, so it cannot say whether A350 deliveries accelerated in Q3. It is kept small for that reason.
findings.independence: Airbus document. Orders from https://www.airbus.com/en/newsroom/press-releases. Shares the programme read with the Boeing finding but is a different OEM.

findings.finding: The Q3 comparison is easy. Q3 2025 sales were $456.2M (commercial aero $274.2M, DS&O $182.0M including an Austrian industrial business divested 2025-09-30), the low quarter of 2025, depressed by A350 destocking. A Q2-like +18% in commercial aero gives about $324M, and total Q3 2026 near $490-505M is +8-11% YoY.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed +8.0% sales and +32% adj EPS YoY: -2.56%. YoY optics have not been paid by themselves.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is inside what the FY guide already tells the market to expect, and the divestiture drag on DS&O is known. Kept because a headline growth print near +10% against the low quarter could still frame the release.
findings.independence: Same Hexcel document family as the guidance finding but a different number (the 2025 Q3 base, not the EPS guide).

findings.finding: Short interest rose 9.0% in the second half of September to 6.45% of float (4.9 days to cover) into the print, while the stock sat near its Oct 9 low.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on record. Not a crowded short (well under the 18-23% levels that squeezed elsewhere).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, not a fact against it. It adds a little convexity to a positive surprise: at 4.9 days a cover on a raise adds some follow-through in the first session.

findings.finding: Hexcel's EVP and Chief Legal and Sustainability Officer exercised options and sold 13,829 shares at about $92.09-92.12 on 2026-09-03, with no 10b5-1 plan box checked, keeping 20,148 shares. The other Form 4s since July are director RSU grants and settlements.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and public. It is an option exercise and sale by a non-operating officer, which usually carries little information. It is filed for completeness, sized small.

findings.finding: In Q2 Hexcel said it is 'now adding headcount and accelerating the restart of previously idle assets', and inventories rose to $345.2M from $328.8M. Cost ahead of volume in the seasonally weakest quarter is a margin risk against Q2's 13.9% adjusted operating margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin has expanded every quarter of 2026 (Q1 13.5%, Q2 13.9%), and the reactions were +4.78% and -2.56%, so the margin line has not yet disappointed.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inference from the company's own words, with no quantified ramp cost. If the market feared it, the skew would lean put, and it is balanced at +1.23. Sized small because it rests on the same document as the EPS-guide finding, read the other way, on the cost line rather than the guide.
findings.independence: Same Hexcel document as the guidance finding. It works against that finding's margin assumption, so the two partly offset.

outside_window.finding: Boeing reports Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-27, and Airbus reports 9M results in late October. Either could reset 787 or A350 rate expectations after the window.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive. The skew is balanced, which neither confirms nor contradicts them, but the +5.6% 20-day rebound and the -2.56% reaction to July's raise cut against a strong upside call, so p_up stays at 55.
lessons_applied: Lessons 1 and 6: no sourced quarterly consensus, and the last guide raise was sold, so the EPS-guide finding went from +0.8 to +0.6
Lesson 5: Collins OE is a counterparty proxy, not Hexcel's number, so it went from +0.5 to +0.4
Lesson 6: the easy comparison lands inside what the FY guide already implies, so it went from +0.3 to +0.1
Lesson 3: the headcount and restart-cost finding shares a document with the guidance finding and partly argues against it, so it went from -0.3 to -0.2
Left standing: GE, Boeing, Airbus, short interest, insider sale; abs_move_pct 5.0 and p_up 55 unchanged
